//: Story Phase 6, chapter 31: The Great Sharkstorm. Survival on deck: flying sharks overhead (their shadows sweep the planks), now and then one coming down on a tile near the captain, always marked first (world/SharkstormLayer.js); brace the shrouds, get Squawks into shelter, heave a shark off the deck together. The storm leans over and drinks the second cloud off the forward deck (cheers); the smell drives the sharks wilder and the storm grows. Then a flying shark comes through the wall by the station and into the S.E.S. ('Ribbit... tax deduction...' POP; THEY'RE ALL GRAY!). At the helm, the breaking point: the labour rule again ('meteorological catastrophe management'), the captain's monologue, and Garrick's answer: 'No.'
p6c7.begin: Something goes over the mast. Then something else. Then a whole shark, upside down, mouth open, very surprised, sailing across the sky from port to starboard.
Its shadow sweeps across the deck. Then the next one's.

p6c7.begin.tutorial: Brace the ship: secure the shrouds (three of them). Watch the deck: a red ring and a growing shadow means a shark is coming down there. Step off it.
p6c7.begin.title: The Great Sharkstorm

then.tutorial: Get Squawks somewhere sheltered (his basket, by the cabin door).
then.title: The Great Sharkstorm

p6c7.rope_a: The starboard shrouds are thrumming like a bass fiddle, one lanyard already loose and whipping.
p6c7.rope_b: The port shrouds. A shark has gone through them once already; two are hanging slack.
p6c7.rope_c: The mizzen braces on the quarterdeck, the yard swinging wild every time the storm breathes in.
p6c7.squawks: captain[determined]: I know. In ye go.
You wedge his basket into the cabin doorway, behind the open door, with Doc Fennimore crouched in front of it.
fennimore[annoyed]: Nothing gets past me, Captain. Not a fin.
p6c7.deck_shark: A whistle, falling. A shadow on the planks midships, growing.
THUMP. A whole shark lands on the deck, midships, right in front of the main hatch, and starts thrashing.

p6c7.deck_shark.tutorial: Shark on deck! Get the crew together and heave it overboard (midships, by the main hatch).
p6c7.deck_shark.title: The Great Sharkstorm

p6c7.heave: Rook, Pete, Brask and Gristle pile in beside you. Eight hands, one shark, a lot of opinions.
The shark goes over the port rail with an expression of deep betrayal.
In the cabin doorway, a small bald head comes up out of the blankets, looks round at the flying sharks, the column, the lightning, and the crew in a heap.
p6c7.absorb: The column of the Great Sharkstorm leans over the ship.
Over the forward deck, the new cloud lifts, stretches, and goes up into it like soup up a straw.
In a few seconds, the forward deck is clear. Clear air. The first clear air on the Revenge in weeks.
crew: IT TOOK THE CLOUD!
pete[happy]: It ATE it! It ATE the CENTER!
gristle[happy]: Best thing a storm's ever done for me!
Then the smell gets into the storm. And the storm gets into the sharks.
The column swells. Turns faster. The sharks in it thrash and snap at each other and the whole thing roars.
gristle[alarmed]: ...Worst thing a storm's ever done for me.
A whistle. Close. Off the port quarter, one shark comes out of the column lower and faster than all the others.
CRASH.
It comes through the rail by the station, straight through the side of the cabinet, and stops, wedged, half in and half out of the Stenchmaster Entertainment System.
Sparks. Smoke. A crackle. The cracked glass flickers green, once.
franklin: Ribbit... tax... deduction...
POP.
The shark works itself loose, flops twice, and slides out through the hole it came in by, into the sea.
garrick[terrified]: NO! NOOOOO! NOT THE S.E.S.!
It is the most upset anyone has seen him. More upset than about the hull. More upset than about the cape.
captain[angry]: A SHARK JUST ATTACKED YOUR TELEVISION.
garrick[annoyed]: I'll have that shark. THAT one. I'll remember its face. I'll find it if it takes me the rest of my life.
captain: Which one?
garrick[offended]: The GRAY one.
crew: THEY'RE ALL GRAY!
The ship heels hard to starboard. Up on the quarterdeck, Nell is losing the wheel.
p6c7.breaking: You take the wheel from Nell. It fights you like a living thing.
Somebody has rigged a blanket into a pouch across your chest. Squawks is in it, with just his head out, like a joey.
The Grand Stenchmaster climbs up onto the quarterdeck, takes a stance at the rail, and raises one gloved hand to the storm.
garrick[proud]: Crew of the Revenge! I have studied this phenomenon, and I can tell you: this storm is POWERED BY CONCENTRATED ODOUR!
jory[annoyed]: The labour rule! Emergency! ONE USEFUL THING!
garrick[businesslike]: Ah. Now. The rule covers emergency LABOUR. This is meteorological and atmospheric catastrophe management. A completely different department.
captain[angry]: That rule was nailed to the MAST, Garrick. It was the one thing. The ONE thing.
garrick[proud]: And I respect it, Captain. I simply have other duties. Releases. Seat warming. The S.E.S. Frog Grog quality assurance. Ceremony. Rest.
rook[annoyed]: The S.E.S. JUST GOT HIT BY A SHARK!

choice.text: Let him have it. All of it. (furious)

then: captain[determined]: Garrick. Listen to me. Very carefully.

choice.text: Count it off on your fingers. (exhausted)
then: captain[tired]: Let me just... go through it. All of it.

choice.text: Laugh, a little bit, the wrong way. (incredulous)
then: captain[surprised]: Hah. Hah hah. Oh, ye want the LIST?

p6c7.breaking: captain[angry]: You attracted every SHARK in the SEA.
captain[angry]: The sharks ATE THE HULL. You ate ROTTEN GARLIC. You fired off every CANNON on the SHIP. The ship is leaking gas through the WOOD.
captain[angry]: And now the sharks are in a STORM. The STORM is made of SHARKS. Because of YOU.
He looks down at his stomach.
He looks up at the Great Sharkstorm.
You scream. It's a good, long, full-chested scream. Somewhere in the column, a shark hears it and swims a little faster.
